text:
caroline.ae: Quick ping — RiverTrust legal wants confirmation that our on-prem POC can be fully air-gapped. They want the package layout, offline upgrade steps, install constraints (OS, ports, disk), compliance artifacts we can share for the POC, and any known enterprise blockers. POC target = 3-node HA. SE/eng/security please chime in.

 tom.se: We do support fully offline POCs. We ship a signed bundle (tarball) with all container images, helm charts, and helper scripts. No outbound required unless they opt for remote support.

 jordan.eng: Example bundle layout we provide:
```
redwood-onprem-2.2.0.tgz
  /images/images.tar        # docker save output (all images)
  /charts/redwood-charts.tgz
  /scripts/install.sh
  /scripts/upgrade.sh
  /scripts/preflight.sh
  /manifests/cosign.sig
  /manifests/checksums.sha512
  /sbom/spdx.json
```
We sign manifests with cosign and include SBOM (SPDX) + checksums for chain-of-custody.

 tom.se: Typical offline install steps ops team runs: 
```
scp redwood-onprem-2.2.0.tgz ops@node:/tmp
ssh ops@node 'sudo tar -xzf /tmp/redwood-onprem-2.2.0.tgz -C /opt/redwood'
/opt/redwood/scripts/preflight.sh --airgap-check
/opt/redwood/scripts/install.sh --airgap --license /opt/redwood/licenses/river.lic
```

 jordan.eng: Key infra constraints to call out to RiverTrust:
- Supported distros: RHEL 8.6+, Ubuntu 20.04/22.04, SLES 15 SP3+. Kernel >= 5.4.
- glibc >= 2.28.
- Memory: min 64GB per node for medium model workloads.
- Disk: baseline 120GB OS + recommended 200GB persistent for model cache; NVMe recommended for KV/cache.
- Required intra-cluster ports: raft 2380, internal RPC 7000-7010, ingress 8443.
- Time sync and DNS must be stable (cert bootstrap fails with >2s drift).

 priya.security: From security POV: we support BYO KMS via PKCS#11 or KMIP. HSM vendor libraries must be installed by the customer (we include connector code in the bundle but not proprietary libs).
- FIPS-compatible images available on request (adds verification time).
- For zero-egress environments remote support is disabled by default; we offer an offline-support plan (signed runbooks + remote jump-host under customer control) if they want vendor-assisted troubleshooting.

 caroline.ae: How do offline upgrades work? They want cadence and risk profile — especially DB/schema migrations and rollback story.

 tom.se: Recommended cadence for customers:
- Security hotfixes: monthly micro-bundles (small image diffs).
- Minor releases: every 6-8 weeks (bug fixes/perf).
- Major releases: opt-in, ~12 months, may include schema migrations.

 jordan.eng: For POC we deliver a pinned bundle. If they request upgrades we provide an upgrade bundle `upgrade-2.2.1.tgz` containing new images and migration scripts. Offline upgrade flow: 
1) run `preflight.sh --upgrade-check` on a control node
2) upload `upgrade-2.2.1.tgz` to `/opt/redwood/upgrades`
3) run `/opt/redwood/scripts/upgrade.sh --rolling --batch 1 --verify`
Default batch=1 for a 3-node cluster. `--verify` runs smoke checks after each node.

 jordan.eng: Rollback plan: snapshot PVs before upgrade (`./backup.sh --out /opt/redwood/backups/<ts>`). If upgrade fails: `./upgrade.sh --rollback --from <ts>`. Node-level pod downtime typically 2-8 minutes; full cluster warmup depends on model cache size and can be 10-40 minutes for very large caches. Call out caches >500GB cause longer rewarm.

 priya.security: Artifacts we can supply for the POC: cosign-signed manifests, SBOM, redacted SLSA build logs, and sha checksums. For SOC2/ISO artifacts we can provide redacted packs under NDA.

 deploy-bot: artifact-signer:redwood-onprem-2.2.0.tgz cosign-sig available at 2026-03-19T12:00:00Z sha512:ef12... sbom:sbom-2.2.0.json

 caroline.ae: Pricing: do we charge for an air-gapped on-prem POC?

 tom.se: POC options: 
- 30-45 day free POC for up to 3 nodes (standard best-effort support).
- White-glove airgap onboarding (bundle prep + install assistance + runbooks): one-time retainer typically $5k-$8k depending on scope.
- Extended eval: 50% list price for 90 days if they need longer trial license.

 caroline.ae: Any enterprise blockers I should flag to RiverTrust security?

 jordan.eng: Common blockers: 
- Unsupported OS (EL7/CentOS7) or old kernels — requires OS uplift.
- HSM vendor agents that cannot be installed in air-gap (closed-source/managed agent) — requires vendor coordination or an integration VM exempt from strict policies.
- Policies that forbid execution of unsigned code; we provide signed manifests but some teams need reproducible-build attestation.

 priya.security: Also flag that FIPS requirements add extra validation time. SAML IdP in strict air-gap often needs a bridging proxy or handshake workaround.

 caroline.ae: Metrics footprint for POC — they are tight on disk.

 tom.se: For POC we usually set metrics retention to 7 days at 5s scrape (~6-12GB/node). If they want 30 days @1s expect ~40-60GB/node; we can tune scrape frequency and retention for the POC.

 jordan.eng: License enforcement: airgap uses a time-bound token file (no phone-home). For long-term we offer KMS-bound license rotation which requires an admin to import signed manifests periodically.

 caroline.ae: Great. I'll draft the questionnaire response with these points and ask if they want cosign signatures + redacted build logs ahead of tomorrow's 11am PT call. @tom.se can you join?

 tom.se: Yep, I'll join. :+1:

 priya.security: I'll prepare a redacted SOC2 pack and a short FIPS checklist.

 caroline.ae: Thanks all — I'll paste the final response here once ready. :rocket:
